note: Every witness drives the REAL production seam. No witness re-implements the estimator. No live provider call is made by any test: every provider is a scripted/recording fake with synthetic credentials only.

boundedCorrection.scope: One bounded correction of four P0 defects and one adjacent P1. No new tracing architecture, no estimator change, no context-threshold change, no compaction-policy change.

defectsCorrected.defect: The 8 MiB / 64 MiB limits did not constrain ACTUAL writes: flush() computed the truncation flag and then wrote the COMPLETE serialized candidate anyway, and successive flushes left obsolete files behind, so the in-memory retention cap did not bound the directory.
defectsCorrected.correction: The oversized candidate is REJECTED BEFORE ANY BYTE IS WRITTEN and reported as a metadata-only rejection receipt. The store tracks the files it owns, derives the byte/count totals from that map, and removes superseded files. chmod corrects the directory and every written file, because mkdir/writeFile mode only applies to newly created entries.
defectsCorrected.red: 3 of 14 capture-store tests FAILED against a deliberately reverted implementation
gates: P0-1: an oversized candidate is REJECTED BEFORE the write — the disk stays bounded
P0-1: repeated captures keep the ACTUAL disk file count and byte total bounded
P0-1: a SUPERSEDED control candidate is REMOVED from disk
P0-3: a PERMISSIVE pre-existing directory and file are CORRECTED, not inherited

defectsCorrected.defect: Fingerprinting ran even with diagnostics disabled: prepareModelRequest() unconditionally built the provider dispatch record, adding a projection, a token estimation, a canonicalization and a synchronous SHA-256 to every ordinary request.
defectsCorrected.correction: The guard is AT THE PRODUCER. isProviderDispatchRecordRequired(sink) (new, in @cline/shared) reports whether any consumer of the dispatch record exists; when it does not, the record is not built at all.
defectsCorrected.red: the P0-2 witness FAILED (1 failed / 7 passed) against a deliberately reverted implementation
gates: P0-2: with NO sink, the dispatch-record projection and fingerprint NEVER execute

defectsCorrected.defect: The private capture was not dogfood-only: the arming function checked only the opt-in variable, and the storage resolver fell back to ~/.cline/data, so a full prompt/tool-argument capture could land in the shared default data directory.
defectsCorrected.correction: Arming requires BOTH the explicit opt-in AND the closed-runtime dogfood identity CLINEMM_RUNTIME_PROFILE=dogfood (exact-match, fail-closed). The storage root resolves ONLY from CLINE_DATA_DIR or <CLINE_DIR>/data; there is no implicit ~/.cline/data fallback and the capture is not armed when neither is set.
defectsCorrected.red: covered by the same 3-of-14 RED run as P0-1
gates: the private capture is armed ONLY by an explicit separate opt-in AND the dogfood identity
P0-3: a REGULAR profile can NEVER arm the capture, even with the opt-in set
P0-3: the storage root FAILS CLOSED — there is no implicit ~/.cline/data fallback

defectsCorrected.defect: The exported latency trace lost the new correlation fields: LatencyTraceSink recorded observation.payload only, while the authoritative preparationRequestId / modelRequestId live on the OBSERVATION, and the finite metadata allowlist did not carry the new fields. The exported JSON therefore could not establish the decision -> dispatch -> completion join.
defectsCorrected.correction: The sink projects the observation identity onto the metadata bag, and the finite LATENCY_METADATA_ALLOWLIST carries preparationRequestId, modelRequestId, decisionId, decisionJoinAuthority, estimatedFinalInputTokens, finalProjectionFingerprint (+ representation/version/producer), providerFamily, providerVisibleMessageCount and toolSchemaCount.
defectsCorrected.red: 4 of 5 export-path tests FAILED against a deliberately reverted implementation
gates: the EXPORTED trace carries the preparation identity through the dispatch and completion
the EXPORTED trace carries the dispatch record's measurement and fingerprint
the EXPORTED trace does NOT leak request CONTENT
the compaction DECISION joins to the dispatch through the preparation identity
the join authority is UNAVAILABLE — never AUTHORITATIVE — when the preparation identity is absent

defectsCorrected.defect: The candidate snapshot was not deep-copied, and the filtered options could diverge from the pre-filter fingerprint: record() retained object references and flush() serialized them later, so a mutation in between could change what the supposedly exact snapshot represented.
defectsCorrected.correction: record() deep-copies and freezes the candidate BEFORE the first asynchronous boundary. The write boundary still re-applies the option allowlist as defence in depth.
defectsCorrected.red: covered by the P1 witness (mutation after record)
gates: P1: the captured snapshot is IMMUTABLE — a later mutation cannot change it

boundedCorrection.nonBlocking: The invalid Leamas gate-summary binding was classified P2, NON-BLOCKING and was deliberately not spent another cycle on.

red.demonstratedGap: Without a forwarded preparation identity the compaction decision carried only its own (sessionId, iteration, decisionOrdinal) identity and NO link to the request it measured; the decisionJoinAuthority is UNAVAILABLE. The decision record also carried NO candidate content, so the exact pre-compaction candidate could not be reconstructed from the metadata.

requiredGateCoverage.requirement: Early request identity survives the prepare-turn/compaction boundary
requiredGateCoverage.evidence: The forwarded preparationRequestId appears verbatim on the decision record; decisionJoinAuthority is AUTHORITATIVE when present and UNAVAILABLE (never synthesized) when absent.

requiredGateCoverage.requirement: Decision and provider dispatch correlate authoritatively for a non-compacting request
requiredGateCoverage.evidence: The submitted and finished records carry the SAME preparationRequestId and the SAME modelRequestId; the dispatch record carries estimatedFinalInputTokens, providerVisibleMessageCount, toolSchemaCount and the finalProjectionFingerprint with its representation/version/producer.

requiredGateCoverage.requirement: Compacted candidates remain distinct from the post-compaction request
requiredGateCoverage.evidence: Two decisions in the SAME iteration retain distinct decisionIds and distinct forwarded preparation identities; the private capture records the candidate BEFORE compaction while the dispatch record fingerprints the FINAL post-compaction projection, so the two are distinguishable by representation.

requiredGateCoverage.requirement: Two provider attempts using one prepared request do not double-count decisions
requiredGateCoverage.evidence: The preparation identity is bound to the PREPARED REQUEST (never re-minted per attempt) and the attempt identity is minted per ATTEMPT and is always distinct from it. The number of preparation identities is <= the number of attempts, so a retry cannot inflate the decision count.

requiredGateCoverage.requirement: beforeModel mutations invalidate false equality assumptions
requiredGateCoverage.evidence: A beforeModel hook that appends a message changes the finalProjectionFingerprint and the providerVisibleMessageCount; the two dispatches are provably different.

requiredGateCoverage.requirement: Actual provider usage joins to the correct attempt, not the nearest timestamp
requiredGateCoverage.evidence: Two consecutive turns produce two distinct attempt identities and two distinct preparation identities; each usage record carries the inputTokens of its OWN attempt (111 vs 222).

requiredGateCoverage.requirement: Missing usage remains unavailable, never zero
requiredGateCoverage.evidence: usageAvailable is false and the inputTokens/outputTokens fields are ABSENT (not zero) when the provider reports no usage.

requiredGateCoverage.requirement: Cache token accounting does not double-count
requiredGateCoverage.evidence: inputTokens (the complete prompt) and cacheReadTokens (a subset) are reported ALONGSIDE each other; the cached amount is never added into the total.

requiredGateCoverage.requirement: The candidate snapshot preserves structured tool results and exact ordering
requiredGateCoverage.evidence: The captured JSON preserves the exact message order, the structured tool_result block with its tool_use_id and its nested content parts (not flattened), the multi-part message parts in order, and the tool inventory order.

requiredGateCoverage.requirement: Truncation makes a snapshot explicitly ineligible for exact replay
requiredGateCoverage.evidence: An over-budget candidate yields truncated=true, snapshotComplete=false and truncationReason=CANDIDATE_EXCEEDS_PER_CANDIDATE_BYTE_BUDGET.

requiredGateCoverage.requirement: Diagnostics OFF adds no capture I/O or serialization
requiredGateCoverage.evidence: The execution result, the reported usage and the dispatched provider-visible message count are IDENTICAL with the diagnostics off. The private capture performs no directory creation, no serialization and no write when its own separate opt-in is absent.

requiredGateCoverage.requirement: Synthetic credentials cannot enter shareable artifacts
requiredGateCoverage.evidence: A credential-shaped option key is absent from the captured payload AND from the receipt; only the allowlisted formatting-relevant options survive. The filter is applied at the producer AND at the write boundary.

requiredGateCoverage.requirement: Capture failures do not change runtime behaviour
requiredGateCoverage.evidence: A capture write failure rejects, and the store's retained candidate state is unchanged (1 retained, 0 written, 0 bytes).

requiredGateCoverage.requirement: The existing compaction threshold and overflow controls are unchanged
requiredGateCoverage.evidence: A tiny request still reports shouldCompact=false and compactionInitiated=false and returns undefined (no compaction); a genuinely oversized request still reports shouldCompact=true and compactionInitiated=true and produces a compacted transcript. The estimator, threshold and compaction-shared files are byte-identical to HEAD.

regressionFoundAndFixed.symptom: 10 production agent-runtime tests timed out (5000ms) after the first implementation, which used an ASYNCHRONOUS WebCrypto digest on the request-preparation path.
regressionFoundAndFixed.mechanism: The digest introduced a suspension point that the production retry-backoff tests, which drive the runtime with FAKE TIMERS, could not advance.
regressionFoundAndFixed.resolution: The fingerprint is computed with a dependency-free SYNCHRONOUS FIPS 180-4 SHA-256 (sdk/packages/shared/src/runtime/compaction-token-evidence.ts). It adds NO suspension point, so the request, the tool inventory, the token budget and the provider dispatch are bit-for-bit identical to the un-instrumented path.
regressionFoundAndFixed.sha256Witness: The synchronous digest is witnessed against node:crypto at every block boundary (lengths 0, 3, 55, 56, 63, 64, 65, 1000, unicode, 100000) in sdk/packages/shared/src/runtime/compaction-token-evidence.test.ts.
